'''Nalin H. Samarasinha''' (born 1958) is a Sri Lankan born [[planetary scientist]] and a [[discoverer of minor planets]], who studies the dynamical evolution and processes of cometary [[Cometary nuclei|nuclei]] and [[Coma (cometary)|comae]].<ref name="MPC-Samarasinha" /> Currently, he works as a senior scientist for the [[Planetary Science Institute]] in the United States.<ref name="sundaytimes" /><ref name="sundaytimes-2" />

== Early life ==

Samarasinha earned a [[Bachelor of Science|BSc]] first class honours in Physics from [[University of Colombo]] after schooling at Hena Vidyalaya, Mt. Lavinia and [[Nalanda College Colombo]].<ref name="dailynews"/> Later he gained a [[Master of Science|MSc]] in astronomy from [[University of Maryland, College Park]] USA and followed it up furthering studies graduating with a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in [[Astronomy]] from the University of Maryland.<ref>[http://www.psi.edu/about/staff/nalin/nalin.html Nalin Samarasinha]</ref>

== Discoveries and honours ==

Florian asteroid [[12871 Samarasinha]] ({{mp|1998 ML|37}}), discovered by astronomers with the [[LONEOS]] survey in 1998, was named in his honor. The official {{MoMP|12871|naming citation}} was published by [[International Astronomical Union|IAU's]] [[Minor Planet Center]] on 24 July 2002 ({{small|[[Minor Planet Circulars|M.P.C.]] 46109}}).<ref name="MPC-Samarasinha" /><ref name="MPC-Circulars-Archive" /> He is the first native born citizen of Sri Lanka to gain the distinction of having an asteroid named after him.<ref name="dailynews"/> Together with astronomer [[Tod R. Lauer]], he is credited with the discovery of asteroid {{LoMP|607372|{{mp|607372 Colombounilanka}}}}.<ref name="MPC-asteroid-607372" />
